items.title: Alvin Queen interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 23, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And I got a call one day from Charles Tolliver during my stint with George Benson in 1971, to go to Europe.

ctx.x: What would it have required of you to do that?

Well I first went to — I never had any dreams really, as far as going to Europe. And I basically always wanted to be involved with different groups and to build my own group. And I spent many, many years as you know, with Horace Silver and George Benson and Wild Bill Davis and Tiny Grimes, and I mean I can go back, oh, Pharoah Sanders — I’ve done some stuff with George Coleman’s recordings, and many different people. And I got a call one day from Charles Tolliver during my stint with George Benson in 1971, to go…
there than I worked in America. And that’s the reason why I travel so much. But I made my — my biggest communication, I believe, was in Europe with the musicians. That’s how I managed to do that.
